findings.evidence: NUMERIC-A1 (P0 must-pass per AUDIT_PLAN §10) is structurally unverified: numeric-grid.json shows all 5 samples with kds_total_text=null, kds_total_parsed=null, delta_centimes=null. Inspecting state 17 KDS DOM confirms KDS order cards render only '1x Tacos M (1 Viande)' (qty + item name) with NO total amount field — see DOM '#100526713 N°A0185 ... N° commande: AUDIT-RUSH-A-038-1778444910782 ... 1x Tacos M (1 Viande)'. Cross-surface comparison receipt-total === KDS-card-total is therefore impossible at this surface. The P0 assertion is vacuous: only DB-vs-receipt was actually verified (state 08 receipt=6.50€ matches DB 6.50€, state 11 receipt=2.00€ matches DB 2.00€), the KDS leg of the triple-equality is unproven.
findings.fix_hint: Either (a) add a total display field to the KDS card template (resources/js/components/admin/kds/KdsCardComponent.vue) so the chef sees the order total — useful for till reconciliation cross-check — and re-run NUMERIC-A1 against that selector; OR (b) reframe NUMERIC-A1 to receipt-vs-DB-vs-OSS (OSS does display totals) and remove the KDS leg; OR (c) cross-check via window.__KDS_STATE / Vuex store rather than DOM scrape. Until one of these lands, the P0 must-pass for Wave A is NOT met.

findings.evidence: Network captures show 4 × HTTP 429 on POST /api/admin/pos across states 09 (×2), 13 (×1), 14 (×1). Console mirrors each as 'Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 429 (Too Many Requests)'. DOM analysis of all three states returned 0 elements with role="alert", 0 visible toasts, 0 alert-info/danger/warning components — the only 'toast' matches were utility class names, not rendered toast instances. State 09 PNG shows the empty POS catalog with NO visible rate-limit feedback; state 14 PNG shows the tracker with NO error indicator. Per REVIEWER_PROTOCOL category 6 (silent_error: 4xx/5xx + no role=alert/.toast/.alert-* visible → P0) and category 10 (unexpected_4xx: 429 NOT in allowlist of {401-logout, 422-validation, 304-cache}) this is a product gap: the POS frontend has no toast/alert wired for 429 on /api/admin/pos. The owner's literal rush-hour mission (50 commandes par caisse) will hit the 60/min pos-order-create bucket during real-world rushes; a cashier seeing the order silently fail with no visible feedback is the exact production-breaking class of defect this audit was commissioned to catch.
findings.fix_hint: Add a 429-specific toast in the POS order-submission handler (resources/js/components/admin/pos/PosBoardComponent.vue or similar — wherever the POST /api/admin/pos response is handled in the Vuex/axios layer). Toast copy suggestion: 'Trop de commandes envoyées en peu de temps. Patientez 1s puis réessayez.' Also wire the global axios interceptor (resources/js/bootstrap.js or app.js) to emit a default toast for any 429 with retry-after hint. Verify by re-running Wave A audit and confirming role=alert renders during the burst window.

findings.evidence: State 17 KDS pile renders the banner 'Liste pleine (50 affichée(s), max. serveur) ; d'autres commandes actives existent peut-être — filtrez par statut ou cherchez un n° de ticket. Voir plus'. Observations.json confirms kds.card_count_total=50 with card_count_matching_prefix=38. The audit mission per AUDIT_PLAN §0 is explicitly to simulate '50 commande par caisse et 50 commande par borne' — i.e. 100 active orders. At that scale, 50 orders are hidden behind a 'Voir plus' link and the chef is instructed to 'filtrez par statut ou cherchez un n° de ticket'. The KDS rendering 50-cap is hit at exactly the load the surface must handle during rush hour. Chefs at peak time should not need to paginate/search to see active orders — that is the surface's reason to exist. The banner is informative and offers remediation, but the cap itself defeats the rush-hour use case. Note: this is a server-side cap (max. serveur), not a client render limit — fixing it requires server-side pagination/streaming, not just bumping a client constant.
findings.fix_hint: Investigate the KDS API endpoint server-side cap (likely in app/Http/Controllers/Admin/KdsOrderController.php or similar — search for limit(50) or take(50) on the orders query). Either (a) raise to 200 minimum for branch-rush scenarios, (b) implement cursor-based pagination so 'Voir plus' loads more without losing position, (c) implement virtual scrolling so the chef sees a continuous list. Trade-off: the cap exists to protect render perf; the right fix combines server cursor + client virtual list rather than just raising the number.

findings.evidence: TIMING-A4 (P1 per AUDIT_PLAN §10) reports p95=310ms but n=2 successful samples out of 7 probes. timing-kds-arrival.json shows 5 of 7 KDS-arrival probes returned null (seq 15, 20, 25, 30, 35 all 'kds_arrival_ms: null'). Observations.json confirms 5 × 'kds_arrival=TIMEOUT'. With 5/7 (71%) of samples unobserved, the p95=310ms claim is misleading — it is computed on the only 2 that completed (237ms, 310ms). The probe likely failed because the polling scraper searches for an order's token in KDS DOM, but the KDS server-side cap of 50 cards means orders pushed past slot 50 are silently dropped from the polling window. The true p95 KDS-arrival latency for orders 15-35 is UNMEASURED. Without verification, the TIMING-A4 P1 assertion is unproven for 5 of 7 samples.
findings.fix_hint: Reframe the timing probe to query the KDS API directly (GET /api/admin/kds-order?token=X) rather than scrape the DOM. Alternately, raise the KDS server cap during audit runs OR widen the polling window beyond the 8s SLA. Cause is audit instrumentation, not (necessarily) a product latency defect — but the audit cannot prove the p95<=8s claim on this evidence.

findings.evidence: Order count gap vs plan: AUDIT_PLAN §1 specifies '12 UI orders/surface drive the full visual + interactive flow' for Wave A; observations.json reports 'ui_orders_posted=3'. Plus, of those 3 claimed UI orders, only 2 actually allocated fiscal sequences (fseq=119 confirmed via state 08 receipt 'N° ticket NF525: 119'; fseq=139 confirmed via state 11 receipt 'N° ticket NF525: 139'). The 3rd UI order (state 12 TPE) per observations.json 'state12-pre: pos-cart not visible — retrying goto, pos_cart_ready=false' was attempted but did NOT confirm. ACTUAL UI orders confirmed = 2, not 3. Total Wave A = 2 UI + 38 API = 40, not the planned 50. 10 missing orders = 20% of the rush-hour simulation never happened. Mission was 'simulation réel ... 50 commande par caisse' — 40 vs 50 is a measurable under-coverage. The 60% under-coverage of the UI flow (only 2 of 12 planned UI orders) is the bigger gap: the wizard / payment / receipt / tracker flow has only been visually-exercised twice.
findings.fix_hint: Round 2 must reach at least 10/12 UI orders OR explicitly document a frozen-zone deferral on state-12 TPE flow if pos-wizard.js race is the blocker. Investigate state-12 cart-empty race: spec line ~720 'state12-pre: pos-cart not visible — retrying goto'. Suspect the wave-A spec navigates back to /admin/pos after a confirm and the cart hasn't yet rehydrated. Fix: await a stable [data-testid='pos-cart-ready'] before continuing the wizard.

findings.evidence: State 17 KDS 'Préparations' sidebar (the kitchen-prep aggregation) shows 'Frites Seules' appearing as THREE separate aggregation rows: (a) 'Frites Seules' with sub-instruction 'FRITES SEULES' qty 4, (b) 'Frites Seules' with no sub-instruction qty 27, (c) 'Frites Seules' with sub-instruction 'Taille : 1 viande' qty 4. The 'Taille : 1 viande' sub-instruction on a FRITES SEULES item is semantically wrong — Frites Seules is a side, not a meat-portion item; the 'Taille : 1 viande' is a Tacos/Burger attribute. This indicates option/composition leakage from parent menu items (e.g. menu formules) into sibling lines, OR aggregation key over-fragments by composition_snapshot keys that include irrelevant fields. A chef seeing 'Frites Seules: 4 (Taille: 1 viande)' is confusing at best, misleading at worst. Triple-aggregation also makes total prep count harder to read (35 vs single '35').
findings.fix_hint: Investigate the kitchen-prep aggregation logic (likely in app/Services/Kds/KdsAggregationService.php or computed in resources/js/components/admin/kds/KdsPreparationsSidebar.vue). For side items (Frites Seules, Boisson Seule), the aggregation key should ignore parent-menu attributes (Taille, Viande variations). Alternative: collapse identical item names that have null/empty options-relevant sub-set.

findings.evidence: Wizard interaction integrity not proven: observations.json reports 'state03: viande_btn_visible=false' and 'state05: jambon_btn_visible=false'. So the UI wizard interactive flow for Tacos M is NOT visually proven by Wave A; only API composition_snapshot is proven (16 Tacos M API orders all have non-null snapshots, see composition-snapshot.json). pos-wizard.js itself is FROZEN-ZONE per CLAUDE.md §7 — wizard defects are deferred. But the audit_integrity issue (assertion claimed but interaction was no-op) is NOT frozen-zone-deferred because it concerns the audit's coverage, not the wizard.
findings.fix_hint: Two paths: (a) AUDIT — fix the wizard interaction selectors in spec (likely use [data-testid='pos-wizard-viande-merguez'] instead of text-match); confirm by re-running and checking 'state03: viande_btn_visible=true'. (b) Accept frozen-zone deferral on visual wizard coverage and rely on API-path composition_snapshot evidence only. Recommend (a) for proper UI flow validation. findings.evidence: KDS state 17 DOM contains the substring 'without — replaced with -->' as visible text on multiple cards (e.g. '1x Tacos M (1 Viande) without — replaced with -->'). This appears to be a Vue template comment marker leaking through as text in the rendered output. Not a classic i18n.key.leak pattern, but it's developer-marker text exposed to end users. Found 4+ instances. Cosmetic (visible only in DOM inspection, may not be rendered as readable text in the PNG), but suggests a Vue commented-out template not fully stripped. Examining the PNG, this artifact may be hidden by CSS — only the prefix 'without' is suspicious. Downgraded to P3 cosmetic pending Round 2 visual confirmation.
findings.fix_hint: Search the KDS card template (resources/js/components/admin/kds/KdsCardComponent.vue or similar) for 'without' and any HTML comment tags emitting text. Likely a v-html or a {{ }} interpolation accidentally including a comment marker.
